/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.

  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.

  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
  writes through a `Units` constructor.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Build

/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))

def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)

/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track
    classes := some classes
    kin := { position := some pos
             heading := some heading
             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
             speed := some speed
             extent := some halfExtent
             pathLength := pathLength } }

/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }

def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }

/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
/-- A lane with its direction and neighbours. -/
def lane (id : RegionId) (boundary : List Vec) (direction : Vec)
    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)
    (leadsTo : Option (List RegionId) := none) (enters : Option RegionId := none) : Structure :=
  { id := id
    kind := .lane
    boundary := some boundary
    lane := some { direction := some direction, leftNeighbour := left, rightNeighbour := right,
                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
                   entersIntersection := enters } }
def point (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (pos : Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }

def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }
def signal (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (shows : List SignalIndication) : Device :=
  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }
def sign (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) : Device := device id kind governs
def speedLimit (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (value : Q) (kind : SpeedSignKind) : Device :=
  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }
def zoneSign (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (kind : ZoneKind) (isEnd : Bool)
    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=
  { device id .zoneSign governs with zoneKind := some kind, isEnd := some isEnd, conditions := conditions }

/-- Occupancy from the geometry: every user inside every region whose boundary contains its position. -/
def occupancyFromGeometry (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
  users.flatMap fun u =>
    match u.kin.position with
    | none => []
    | some p => structures.filterMap fun st =>
      match st.boundary with
      | some poly => if Geom.inPolygon p poly then some (u.track, st.id) else none
      | none => none

/-- A scene; occupancy is derived from geometry unless given. -/
def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
  { t := t
    subject := subject
    users := users
    structures := structures
    devices := devices
    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
    env := env
    assumptions := assumptions
    intents := intents }

/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
  (List.range n).map fun k =>
    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    f k t

/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
  | some first, some last =>
    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
    pre ++ τ ++ post
  | _, _ => τ

def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ

/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

end Build

/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
    far enough to decide it. -/
structure Scenario where
  name : String
  rule : String
  trace : Trace
  reading : Reading
  manifest : Manifest
  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
  expected : Verdict
  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
  boundary : String := ""
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace Scenario
/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
def pastOps : List String :=
  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
   "heading_since"]

/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
    `unknown` witness only.
    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
    | .ok S => pure S
    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
    match sc.window with
    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
    | none => true
  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
  match sc.expected with
  | .notApplicable =>
    if tl.present then pure got
    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
  | .unknown _ =>
    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
    if !stray.isEmpty then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
    else pure got
  | _ => pure got
end Scenario

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TRAINING SPLIT variant, generated by harness/tools/split.py from the full file: the lines that read the
3	  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.
4	-/
5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest
7	  What a source can observe: a capability per atom id, complete over ATOMS.md (`subject` is an atom
8	  observed for the subject track alone, as an instrumented vehicle reports its own controls); a mask
9	  that blanks every field of an absent atom, and of a subject-only atom on every other road user,
10	  before evaluation; and `support`, the first and most honest number
11	  a source gets — which rules it can be judged against at all, computed from the rules' syntax
12	  before any frame is read.
13	
14	  The same rules run on a simulator, on an annotated dataset and on perception over video; the
15	  only thing that differs is what each can see, and that difference is a declared input here.
16	  For the perception stage the manifest is the interface the other way round: the list of atoms
17	  its programs must deliver, with the error class each is allowed.
18	-/
19	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
20	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
21	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Ontology.Ids
22	
23	namespace TrafficSpec
24	
25	inductive Capability
26	  | exact
27	  | estimate (errorClass : String)
28	  | absent
29	  | subject
30	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
31	
32	structure Manifest where
33	  source : String
34	  entries : List (String × Capability)     -- atom id in ATOMS.md form ↦ capability
35	  /-- The longest tracker break the source's re-identification links may bridge (seconds). -/
36	  reidGap : Q := Q.zero
37	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
38	
39	namespace Manifest
40	/-- An atom the manifest does not list is absent: silence is not a capability. -/
41	def capability (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Capability :=
42	  ((m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).map (·.2)).getD .absent
43	def observes (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Bool := m.capability id != .absent
44	/-- Complete: every atom id of ATOMS.md has an entry, and no entry names anything else. -/
45	def complete (m : Manifest) : Bool :=
46	  atomIds.all (fun id => (m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).isSome) &&
47	  m.entries.all (fun e => atomIds.contains e.1)
48	def absentIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => !m.observes id
49	/-- The atoms observed for the subject track only. -/
50	def subjectIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => m.capability id == .subject
51	/-- A manifest that observes everything exactly (the simulator's, and the tests'). -/
52	def full (source : String) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
53	  { source := source, entries := atomIds.map fun id => (id, .exact), reidGap := gap }
54	end Manifest
55	
56	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	-- From Lean names back to atom ids
58	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	/-- The atom id a Lean name reads: the longest id whose `defName` is a prefix of the name
60	    (`dev_traffic_signal_shows` ↦ `dev.traffic_signal`), with the relation aliases spelled out. -/
61	def atomIdOf (name : String) : Option String :=
62	  let n := match name with
63	    | "rel_ahead_in_lane" | "rel_behind_in_lane" => "rel_ahead_behind_in_lane"
64	    | other => other
65	  let cands := atomIds.filter fun id =>
66	    let d := Semantics.defName id
67	    n == d || n.startsWith (d ++ "_")
68	  cands.foldl (fun acc id => match acc with
69	    | none => some id
70	    | some a => if id.length > a.length then some id else some a) none
71	
72	/-- The atom ids a read of `id` depends on: itself, and for a read of a region kind or of a relation
73	    that reads kind membership, the kinds whose masks its verdict follows (a kind's ancestors; a
74	    lane relation's lane kind; an entrance's line kinds, stop line and crosswalk). No source
75	    declares an abstract kind: a read of one depends on the kinds refining it directly, and no read
76	    depends on an abstract ancestor. -/
77	def kindDependencies (id : String) : List String :=
78	  let kinds (ks : List StructureKind) := (ks.filter (!·.isAbstract)).map fun k => s!"st.{k}"
79	  let ofKind (k : StructureKind) :=
80	    if k.isAbstract then kinds (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k))
81	    else kinds (k :: k.ancestors)
82	  match id with
83	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => id :: ofKind .lane
84	  | "st.entrance_of" => id :: ofKind .stopLine ++ ofKind .crosswalk
85	  | _ =>
86	    if id.startsWith "st." then
87	      match StructureKind.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
88	      | some k => ofKind k
89	      | none => [id]
90	    else [id]
91	
92	/-- The atom ids a formula list reads, through atoms and primitives (a concept call is expanded first). -/
93	def formulaAtomIds (fs : List Formula) : List String :=
94	  ((fs.flatMap Formula.atoms).flatMap fun n =>
95	    if n.startsWith "prim_" then (Primitives.reads n).filterMap atomIdOf
96	    else (atomIdOf n).toList).flatMap kindDependencies |>.eraseDups
97	
98	/-- The atom ids a rule reads, through its atoms, its primitives and, transitively, the
99	    rules it composes. -/
100	def Rule.atomIds (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List String :=
101	  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (r : Rule) : List String :=
102	    match fuel with
103	    | 0 => formulaAtomIds r.formulas
104	    | fuel + 1 =>
105	      formulaAtomIds r.formulas ++ (r.composes.flatMap fun id =>
106	        if seen.contains id then [] else
107	        match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
108	        | some r' => go fuel (id :: seen) r'
109	        | none => [])
110	  (go rules.length [r.id] r).eraseDups
111	
112	inductive Support
113	  | supported
114	  | partially (absent : List String)      -- some atoms unobserved: verdicts may be unknown
115	  | unsupported (absent : List String)    -- the obligation reads nothing the source observes
116	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
117	
118	def Support.tag : Support → String
119	  | .supported => "supported"
120	  | .partially _ => "partial"
121	  | .unsupported _ => "unsupported"
122	def Support.absent : Support → List String
123	  | .supported => []
124	  | .partially a | .unsupported a => a
125	
126	/-- Support from syntax alone, closed over the rules a rule composes. Unsupported when every atom
127	    the obligation reads is absent (the rule could never decide), or a binder's class can never be
128	    established, or a composed rule is itself unsupported. -/
129	def support (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (m : Manifest) : Support :=
130	  -- the clock is every source's: a window over time reads it, and no manifest declares it absent
131	  let absentOf (fs : List Formula) : List String × Nat :=
132	    let ids := (formulaAtomIds fs).filter (· != "kin.time")
133	    (ids.filter fun id => !m.observes id, ids.length)
134	  let (oblAbsent, oblTotal) := absentOf [r.obligation]
135	  let clsDead := r.binders.any fun b =>
136	    let (a, n) := absentOf [b.cls]
137	    n > 0 && a.length == n
138	  let composedDead := (r.composes.filterMap fun id => rules.find? (·.id == id)).any fun r' =>
139	    let (a, n) := absentOf [r'.obligation]
140	    n > 0 && a.length == n
141	  let allAbsent := (Rule.atomIds rules r).filter fun id => !m.observes id
142	  if allAbsent.isEmpty then .supported
143	  else if clsDead || composedDead || (oblTotal > 0 && oblAbsent.length == oblTotal) then .unsupported allAbsent
144	  else .partially allAbsent
145	
146	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
147	-- Masking: a scene as the source would have produced it
148	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	namespace Mask
150	def user (id : String) (u : RoadUser) : RoadUser :=
151	  match id with
152	  | "ru.subject" => u
153	  | "ru.occupant_count" => { u with occupants := none }
154	  | "ru.rider_posture" => { u with posture := {} }
155	  | "kin.position" => { u with kin := { u.kin with position := none } }
156	  | "kin.heading" => { u with kin := { u.kin with heading := none } }
157	  | "kin.velocity" => { u with kin := { u.kin with velocity := none } }
158	  | "kin.speed" => { u with kin := { u.kin with speed := none } }
159	  | "kin.accel_longitudinal" => { u with kin := { u.kin with accelLongitudinal := none } }
160	  | "kin.yaw_rate" => { u with kin := { u.kin with yawRate := none } }
161	  | "kin.extent" => { u with kin := { u.kin with extent := none } }
162	  | "kin.steer_angle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with steerAngle := none } }
163	  | "kin.path_length" => { u with kin := { u.kin with pathLength := none } }
164	  | "kin.engine_running" => { u with kin := { u.kin with engineRunning := none } }
165	  | "kin.parking_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with parkingBrake := none } }
166	  | "kin.gear" => { u with kin := { u.kin with gear := none } }
167	  | "kin.throttle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with throttle := none } }
168	  | "kin.service_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with serviceBrake := none } }
169	  | "sig.turn_indicator" => { u with sig := { u.sig with turnIndicator := none } }
170	  | "sig.brake_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with brakeLamp := none } }
171	  | "sig.hazard" => { u with sig := { u.sig with hazard := none } }
172	  | "sig.headlamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with headlamp := none } }
173	  | "sig.position_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with positionLamp := none } }
174	  | "sig.warning_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with warningLamps := none } }
175	  | "sig.siren" => { u with sig := { u.sig with siren := none } }
176	  | "sig.horn" => { u with sig := { u.sig with horn := none } }
177	  | "sig.hand_signal" => { u with sig := { u.sig with handSignal := none } }
178	  | "ru.aggregate" => { u with classes := none }   -- the source classifies nothing: every member unknown
179	  | "sig.door_open" => { u with sig := { u.sig with doorsOpen := none } }
180	  | "sig.compression_brake" => { u with sig := { u.sig with compressionBrake := none } }
181	  | "st.sight_along_way" => { u with sightAlongWay := none }
182	  | _ =>
183	    -- a class atom: the source cannot tell this class, so no user is known to have or lack it,
184	    -- nor the attribute the class carries
185	    match RoadUserClass.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
186	    | some k =>
187	      let u := { u with classes := u.classes.map (·.filter (· != k)), unobservedClasses := k :: u.unobservedClasses }
188	      match k with
189	      | .emergencyVehicle => { u with emergencyKind := none }
190	      | .officialVehicle => { u with officialKind := none }
191	      | .electricBicycle => { u with eBikeClass := none }
192	      | _ => u
193	    | none => u
194	
195	def structure' (id : String) (st : Structure) : Option Structure :=
196	  match id with
197	  | "st.lane_direction" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with direction := none } }
198	  | "st.lane_adjacency" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l =>
199	      { l with leftNeighbour := none, rightNeighbour := none, ordinalFromLeft := none, countInDirection := none } }
200	  | "st.lane_connectivity" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with leadsTo := none } }
201	  | "st.lane_enters" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with entersIntersection := none } }
202	  | "st.lane_marking" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with markingLeft := none, markingRight := none } }
203	  | "st.lane_width" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with width := none } }
204	  | "st.curvature" => some { st with curvature := none }
205	  | "st.grade" => some { st with grade := none }
206	  | "st.sight_distance" => some { st with sightDistance := none }
207	  | "st.on_way" => some { st with ways := none }
208	  | "st.entrance_of" => some { st with entranceOf := [], entranceObserved := false }
209	  | "st.region_geometry" => some { st with position := none, boundary := none }
210	  | _ =>

221	  | "dev.position" => some { d with position := none }

223	  | _ =>

233	  | "env.wet_road" => { e with wetRoad := none }
234	  | "env.ice_or_snow" => { e with iceOrSnow := none }

236	  | "env.civil_time" => { e with civilTime := none }
237	  | _ => e

239	def relation (id : String) (m : MeasuredRelation) : MeasuredRelation :=

242	  | "rel.surface_gap" => { m with surfaceGap := none }
243	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => { m with aAheadOfB := none }
244	  | "rel.longitudinal_overlap" => { m with longitudinalOverlap := none }
245	  | "rel.oncoming" => { m with oncoming := none }
246	  | "rel.same_direction" => { m with sameDirection := none }
247	  | "rel.bearing" => { m with bearing := none }
248	  | "rel.contact" => { m with contact := none }
249	  | "rel.visible" => { m with visible := none }
250	  | _ => m

253	    would be computed from only when the source lacks those too; a measured value is dropped. -/
254	def scene (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
255	  match id with
256	  | "ru.subject" => { s with subject := none }
257	  | "rel.occupies" => { s with occupancyObserved := [], occupies := [] }
258	  | "kin.time" => s
259	  | _ =>

261	             structures := s.structures.filterMap (structure' id)
262	             devices := s.devices.filterMap (device id)
263	             env := env id s.env
264	             relations := s.relations.map (relation id) }
265	
266	/-- Blank one atom on every road user but the subject, and in every measured relation not taken
267	    from the subject: what a source that instruments the subject's vehicle alone can say. -/
268	def sceneExceptSubject (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
269	  { s with users := s.users.map fun u => if s.subject == some u.track then u else user id u
270	           relations := s.relations.map fun m => if s.subject == some m.a then m else relation id m }

    (.and (.atom "st_highway" [hw2R] [])

    applicability := applicability
    obligation := obligation
    assumptions := []
    intentions := []
    operationalizations :=

          concepts := ["dev.temporary_traffic_control", "kin.speed", "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane", "rel.occupies", "rel.surface_gap", "st.obstruction", "st.roadway"]
          params := ["p.conditions_permit_min_speed", "p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users"]
          convention := "Traffic-flow feasibility convention (free-flow versus congested operation in highway capacity practice): leaving and holding a long space ahead is possible only where the stream runs freely and nothing occupies the space.           surrogate := false } ]
    residues := ["The purpose clause explains the figure the law itself fixes: the space is 500 feet, and the words “so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger” state what that space is for, adding no further requirement to the duty, which is met by leaving the stated space and breached by not leaving it. The ontology reads a purpose through the conduct it explains, and here that conduct is the leaving of the space the next words measure. The rule is held to this: no verdict of the node turns on these words."]  -- the node's, verbatim; not yours to change
    narrowings :=
      [ { span := "s3"
          why := "The standard's words relieve the duty where a works zone or an obstruction lies in the space between the two bodies. The atoms this operationalization claims place no structure region and no device within that space: rel.occupies relates a road user to a region, rel.surface_gap two road users, and the node claims neither st.region_geometry nor dev.governs nor dev.position. The two leaves are therefore read at the coarsest place those atoms reach — an st.obstruction region lying on the highway the subject's lane lies on, and a dev.temporary_traffic_control device present at the observation — so the conditions are read as not permitting in some scenes where the words would still require the space."
          kind := "reading" } ]
    surrogate := false }

end TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_127_2

  .or (.cmp (laneCount lnR) .ge twoLanes)
    (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln2"

        (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [ln2R, hwR] [])

/-

  y from −12 m to +12 m), an improved roadway on it (region 13) and lanes on it: region 11, the
  eastbound lane (y from −4 m to 0, direction east), region 12, the westbound lane (y from 0 to
  +4 m, direction west), and, where a scene needs a second lane of the subject's direction, region
  14 (y from −8 m to −4 m, direction east). Every lane and the roadway record the highway as their
  way. On the two-lane highway each lane records ordinal 1 of a count of 1 lane in its direction,
  so the count of s7 is decided, not merely unobserved.

  The bodies. An articulated lorry is 18 m long and 2.5 m wide (half-extents 9 m, 1.25 m, 2 m) and
  carries the truck and trailer-or-combination classes, so the truck aggregate holds of it; a
  passenger car is 4.8 m long and 1.78 m (70 inches) wide; a van is 5 m long and 1.8 m wide. All
  run in the eastbound lane on its centre line (y = −2 m), headings east.

  The instants. Each trace is three observations one second apart, the scene unchanged: the rule
  looks back nowhere, so no window needs padding and no witness names one.

  The figures that matter against the reading: a centre spacing of 60 m between two lorries is a
  longitudinal clearance of 42 m, far below the 500 feet (152.4 m) of s4; a centre spacing of
  260 m is a clearance of 242 m, far above it. 22 m/s is far above the free-flow bound of the

def ln2R : Arg := .var "ln2"
def hw2R : Arg := .var "hw2"

def vehicleAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []

  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] []

import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_127_2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

/-- The quantified variables: the followed road user, an overtaken road user, a road user in the
    space, the highway and lanes of s7, the roadway and the obstruction of s3. -/
def uU : Arg := .var "u"
def wW : Arg := .var "w"
def hwR : Arg := .var "hw"
def lnR : Arg := .var "ln"
def ln2R : Arg := .var "ln2"
def hw2R : Arg := .var "hw2"
def ln3R : Arg := .var "ln3"
def rdR : Arg := .var "rd"
def obR : Arg := .var "ob"
def ttcD : Arg := .var "ttc"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/
def pConditionsPermitMaxInterveningUsers : Term := .param "p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users"
def pConditionsPermitMinSpeed : Term := .param "p.conditions_permit_min_speed"
def pOvertakingMinSpeedExcess : Term := .param "p.overtaking_min_speed_excess"
def pSameDirectionCosineTolerance : Term := .param "p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance"
def pStandstillSpeedTolerance : Term := .param "p.standstill_speed_tolerance"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

/-- The text's own figures. -/
def eightyInches : Term := .lit (Units.inches 80) .metre
def fiveHundredFeet : Term := .lit (Units.feet 500) .metre
def twoLanes : Term := .lit (Units.ratio 2 1) .count

-- The admitted aggregates the node claims, each by its id.
def truckAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck"] []
def combinationAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles"] []
def vehicleAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []
def trafficAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] []

/-- The overall width the words measure: `kin.extent`'s width read, which is the full width. -/
def overallWidth (x : Arg) : Term := .measure "kin_extent" [x, .lit "width"]

/-- s1 and s2: a truck of the truck aggregate, or a combination of that aggregate 80 inches or
    more in overall width. -/
def truckOrWideCombination (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .or (truckAggregate x)
    (.and (combinationAggregate x) (.cmp (overallWidth x) .ge eightyInches))

/-- The space between the two bodies, along the subject's heading. -/
def gapAhead (a b : Arg) : Term := .measure "rel_surface_gap" [a, b, .lit "longitudinal"]
/-- `a` is ahead of `b` in the lane the two share. -/
def aheadInLane (a b : Arg) : Formula := .atom "rel_ahead_behind_in_lane" [a, b] []
def speedOf (x : Arg) : Term := .measure "kin_speed" [x]

def following (a b : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_interaction_following" [a, b] [pSameDirectionCosineTolerance]
def overtaking (a b : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_interaction_overtaking" [a, b] [pSameDirectionCosineTolerance, pOvertakingMinSpeedExcess]
def standstill (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_motion_standstill" [x] [pStandstillSpeedTolerance]

/-- Class of `v`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, kin.extent -/
def clsV : Formula := truckOrWideCombination vV

/-- s2: the subject is following another truck or wide combination. -/
def followsWideTruck : Formula :=
  .existsUser "u"
    (.and (.not (.same vV uU))
      (.and (truckOrWideCombination uU) (following vV uU)))

/-- s6: the subject is overtaking and passing a vehicle or a combination of vehicles. -/
def overtakingAnyVehicle : Formula :=
  .existsUser "w"
    (.and (.not (.same vV wW))
      (.and (.or (vehicleAggregate wW) (combinationAggregate wW)) (overtaking vV wW)))

/-- The count of lanes in a lane's direction of travel. -/
def laneCount (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_adjacency" [ln, .lit "count"]
def laneDirectionX (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [ln, .lit "x"]
def laneDirectionY (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [ln, .lit "y"]

/-- s7: two or more lanes of the highway `hw` run in the direction of travel of the lane `ln` the
    subject occupies — the lane's recorded count in that direction is at least two, or another lane
    on the same highway carries the same direction. -/
def twoOrMoreLanesInDirection : Formula :=
  .or (.cmp (laneCount lnR) .ge twoLanes)
    (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln2"
      (.and (.atom "st_lane" [ln2R] [])
        (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [ln2R, hwR] [])
          (.and (.not (.same lnR ln2R))
            (.and (.cmp (laneDirectionX ln2R) .eq (laneDirectionX lnR))
                  (.cmp (laneDirectionY ln2R) .eq (laneDirectionY lnR)))))))

/-- s7: the subject, a vehicle or a combination and a member of traffic, is moving on a highway on
    which two or more lanes are available for traffic moving in its direction. -/
def movingOnMultiLaneHighway : Formula :=
  .and (.or (vehicleAggregate vV) (combinationAggregate vV))
    (.and (.not (standstill vV))
      (.and (trafficAggregate vV)
        (.existsRegion (.lit "highway") "hw"
          (.and (.atom "st_highway" [hwR] [])
            (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln"
              (.and (.atom "st_lane" [lnR] [])
                (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, lnR] [])
                  (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [lnR, hwR] [])
                        twoOrMoreLanesInDirection))))))))

/-- Applicability: s2 (trigger): which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,; s5 (condition): so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,; s6 (exception): but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.; s7 (exception): This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction. -/
def applicability : Formula :=
  .and followsWideTruck
    (.and (.not overtakingAnyVehicle) (.not movingOnMultiLaneHighway))

/-- s3: the road users that occupy a roadway of the subject's and lie in the space between the
    subject and the road user `u` it follows. `count` reads no value of its term, so the term is
    zero. -/
def interveningUsers (u : Arg) : Term :=
  .aggregate .count "w"
    (.and (.not (.same wW vV))
      (.and (.not (.same wW u))
        (.and (.existsRegion (.lit "roadway") "rd"
                (.and (.atom "st_roadway" [rdR] [])
                  (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, rdR] [])
                        (.atom "rel_occupies" [wW, rdR] []))))
          (.and (aheadInLane wW vV)
                (.cmp (gapAhead vV wW) .lt (gapAhead vV u))))))
    zeroMetres

/-- s3: no obstruction lies on the highway the subject's lane lies on (the narrowing declared
    below: the claimed atoms place no region within the space itself). -/
def noObstructionOnTheWay : Formula :=
  .not (.existsRegion (.lit "highway") "hw2"
    (.and (.atom "st_highway" [hw2R] [])
      (.and (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln3"
              (.and (.atom "st_lane" [ln3R] [])
                (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, ln3R] [])
                      (.atom "st_on_way" [ln3R, hw2R] []))))
            (.existsRegion (.lit "obstruction") "ob"
              (.and (.atom "st_obstruction" [obR] [])
                    (.atom "st_on_way" [obR, hw2R] []))))))

/-- s3 (the operationalization "whenever conditions permit"). The convention's third leaf, that no
    `dev.temporary_traffic_control` lies in the space, is not written: see the header and
    `task_result.md` — the node claims no atom that ties a device to the subject or to a region, so
    a device quantifier would range over every device of the scene. -/
def conditionsPermit (u : Arg) : Formula :=
  .and (.cmp (speedOf vV) .ge pConditionsPermitMinSpeed)
    (.and (.cmp (interveningUsers u) .le pConditionsPermitMaxInterveningUsers)
          noObstructionOnTheWay)

/-- Obligation: s3 (standard): shall, whenever conditions permit,; s4 (obligation): leave a space of 500 feet -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallUser "u"
    (.implies
      (.and (.not (.same vV uU))
        (.and (truckOrWideCombination uU)
          (.and (following vV uU) (aheadInLane uU vV))))
      (.implies (conditionsPermit uU) (.cmp (gapAhead vV uU) .ge fiveHundredFeet)))

def rule : Rule :=
  { id := "NRS_484B_127_2"
    laws := ["NRS-484B-127-2"]
    binders :=
      [ { name := "v", cls := clsV } ]
    applicability := applicability
    obligation := obligation
    assumptions := []
    intentions := []
    operationalizations :=
      [ { standard := "whenever conditions permit"

  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck"] []
def combinationAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles"] []
def vehicleAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []
def trafficAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] []

/-
  NRS_484B_127_2 — NRS-484B-127-2

  THE READING (the blueprint's; the coding session records here, per span, how each element,
  operationalization and composition below is written, and every choice the text did not dictate).

  Spans:
    s1 (subject): The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
    s2 (trigger): which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
    s3 (standard): shall, whenever conditions permit,
    s4 (obligation): leave a space of 500 feet
    s5 (condition): so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,
    s6 (exception): but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.
    s7 (exception): This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.

  Elements (span → atoms, derived):
    s1: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'kin.extent'], derived []
    s2: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'kin.extent'], derived ['drv.interaction.following']
    s4: atoms ['rel.surface_gap', 'rel.ahead_behind_in_lane'], derived []
    s6: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle'], derived ['drv.interaction.overtaking']
    s7: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic', 'st.highway', 'st.lane', 'st.lane_adjacency', 'st.lane_direction', 'st.on_way', 'rel.occupies'], derived ['drv.motion.standstill']

  Literals the text states (each written through its Units constructor):
    s1: 80 in — 80 inches
    s2: 80 in — 80 inches
    s4: 500 ft — 500 feet
    s7: 2 count — two

  No magnitude below is this file's own: parameters name the reading, literals are the text's.

  HOW EACH SPAN IS WRITTEN

  s1 (the binder's class, `clsV`). `truckOrWideCombination v`: the admitted aggregate
  DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, or the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles
  with the read width (`kin_extent`, component `width`, which the vocabulary reads as the full
  width) at least the text's 80 inches. The qualifier "80 inches or more in overall width" is
  attached to the combination limb, as the record's `applicability` states it. "The driver of" is
  the record's own observable reading (agency) and is not restated in `narrowings`.

  s2 (`followsWideTruck`, in the applicability). Some road user other than the subject
  (`.not (.same v u)`) is itself a truck of that aggregate or a combination of that width, and the
  subject is following it (`drv.interaction.following`, the same-direction tolerance of the
  reading). The followed road user is quantified, not bound: the duty exists for the subject
  whether or not a scene supplies one.

  s3 (`conditionsPermit`, the operationalization, in the obligation). The subject's `kin_speed`
  at least `p.conditions_permit_min_speed`; the count of other road users that occupy a roadway
  the subject occupies (`st.roadway` with `rel.occupies`), lie ahead of the subject in its lane
  (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`) and lie nearer than the followed road user (the longitudinal
  component of `rel.surface_gap`), at most `p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users`; and no
  `st.obstruction` on the way (see the narrowing below). The convention's fourth leaf, that no
  `dev.temporary_traffic_control` lies in the space, is not written at all: the node claims no atom
  that relates a device to the subject or to a region (`dev.governs` and `dev.position` are atoms
  of the surface, and this node claims neither), so a device quantifier would range over every
  device of the scene, the subject's or not. That is a defect of the node's mapping, not a reading
  open to me, and it is reported rather than declared here.

  s4 (the obligation). For every road user the subject is following in the sense of s2 and that is
  ahead of it in its lane (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`, the s4 claim that fixes which space is
  meant), where the conditions of s3 permit, the longitudinal component of `rel.surface_gap`
  between the two bodies is at least the text's 500 feet. The obligation re-selects the followed
  road user with the whole of s2's selection, since the applicability's binding does not reach it.
  The record's reading of "a space of 500 feet" as that longitudinal clearance is the plan's
  narrowing on s4 and is not restated here.

  s5 is the record's residue: no verdict turns on it.

  s6 (`overtakingAnyVehicle`, negated in the applicability). Some road user other than the subject
  is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or a combination of DEF-NRS-484A-050, and the subject
  is passing it (`drv.interaction.overtaking`, with the reading's same-direction tolerance and
  minimum speed excess). The overtaking road user is the subject, whose class s1 already fixes.

  s7 (`movingOnMultiLaneHighway`, negated in the applicability). The subject is a vehicle or a
  combination; it is not at a standstill (`drv.motion.standstill`, the posted definition of a
  complete cessation from movement, negated for "while moving"); it is traffic
  (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), which fixes whose movement the lanes are available for; and it
  occupies (`rel.occupies`) a lane (`st.lane`) that lies on a highway (`st.on_way`, `st.highway`)
  on which two or more lanes run in that lane's direction of travel. The last is read from the two
  observations the claimed atoms carry of that one fact: the lane's recorded count of lanes in its
  direction (`st.lane_adjacency`, field `count`) is at least the text's two, or another lane on the
  same highway carries the same direction of travel (`st.lane_direction`, both components). Either
  observation establishes the fact the words state; neither adds a requirement to it, and the
  direction read is the one the subject travels in because it is the direction of the lane the
  subject occupies.

  s3: "no obstruction lies in that space". The atoms the node claims for this standard carry no
  relation that places a structure region within the space between two bodies: `rel.occupies`
  relates a road user to a region, `rel.surface_gap` two road users, and the node claims no
  `st.region_geometry`. The leaf is therefore read at the coarsest place those atoms reach: an
  `st.obstruction` region that lies on the highway the subject's lane lies on makes the conditions
  not permit, so the reading relieves the duty in some scenes where the words would relieve it only
  for an obstruction in the space itself.

import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_127_2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

/-- The quantified variables: the followed road user, an overtaken road user, a road user in the
    space, the highway and lanes of s7, the roadway and the obstruction of s3. -/
def uU : Arg := .var "u"
def wW : Arg := .var "w"
def hwR : Arg := .var "hw"
def lnR : Arg := .var "ln"
def ln2R : Arg := .var "ln2"
def hw2R : Arg := .var "hw2"
def ln3R : Arg := .var "ln3"
def rdR : Arg := .var "rd"
def obR : Arg := .var "ob"
def ttcD : Arg := .var "ttc"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/
def pConditionsPermitMaxInterveningUsers : Term := .param "p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users"
def pConditionsPermitMinSpeed : Term := .param "p.conditions_permit_min_speed"
def pOvertakingMinSpeedExcess : Term := .param "p.overtaking_min_speed_excess"
def pSameDirectionCosineTolerance : Term := .param "p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance"
def pStandstillSpeedTolerance : Term := .param "p.standstill_speed_tolerance"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

/-- The text's own figures. -/
def eightyInches : Term := .lit (Units.inches 80) .metre
def fiveHundredFeet : Term := .lit (Units.feet 500) .metre
def twoLanes : Term := .lit (Units.ratio 2 1) .count

-- The admitted aggregates the node claims, each by its id.
def truckAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck"] []
def combinationAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles"] []
def vehicleAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []
def trafficAggregate (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .atom "ru_aggregate" [x, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"] []

/-- The overall width the words measure: `kin.extent`'s width read, which is the full width. -/
def overallWidth (x : Arg) : Term := .measure "kin_extent" [x, .lit "width"]

/-- s1 and s2: a truck of the truck aggregate, or a combination of that aggregate 80 inches or
    more in overall width. -/
def truckOrWideCombination (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .or (truckAggregate x)
    (.and (combinationAggregate x) (.cmp (overallWidth x) .ge eightyInches))

/-- The space between the two bodies, along the subject's heading. -/
def gapAhead (a b : Arg) : Term := .measure "rel_surface_gap" [a, b, .lit "longitudinal"]
/-- `a` is ahead of `b` in the lane the two share. -/
def aheadInLane (a b : Arg) : Formula := .atom "rel_ahead_behind_in_lane" [a, b] []
def speedOf (x : Arg) : Term := .measure "kin_speed" [x]

def following (a b : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_interaction_following" [a, b] [pSameDirectionCosineTolerance]
def overtaking (a b : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_interaction_overtaking" [a, b] [pSameDirectionCosineTolerance, pOvertakingMinSpeedExcess]
def standstill (x : Arg) : Formula :=
  .derived "drv_motion_standstill" [x] [pStandstillSpeedTolerance]

/-- Class of `v`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, kin.extent -/
def clsV : Formula := truckOrWideCombination vV

/-- s2: the subject is following another truck or wide combination. -/
def followsWideTruck : Formula :=
  .existsUser "u"
    (.and (.not (.same vV uU))
      (.and (truckOrWideCombination uU) (following vV uU)))

/-- s6: the subject is overtaking and passing a vehicle or a combination of vehicles. -/
def overtakingAnyVehicle : Formula :=
  .existsUser "w"
    (.and (.not (.same vV wW))
      (.and (.or (vehicleAggregate wW) (combinationAggregate wW)) (overtaking vV wW)))

/-- The count of lanes in a lane's direction of travel. -/
def laneCount (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_adjacency" [ln, .lit "count"]
def laneDirectionX (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [ln, .lit "x"]
def laneDirectionY (ln : Arg) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [ln, .lit "y"]

/-- s7: two or more lanes of the highway `hw` run in the direction of travel of the lane `ln` the
    subject occupies — the lane's recorded count in that direction is at least two, or another lane
    on the same highway carries the same direction. -/
def twoOrMoreLanesInDirection : Formula :=
  .or (.cmp (laneCount lnR) .ge twoLanes)
    (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln2"
      (.and (.atom "st_lane" [ln2R] [])
        (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [ln2R, hwR] [])
          (.and (.not (.same lnR ln2R))
            (.and (.cmp (laneDirectionX ln2R) .eq (laneDirectionX lnR))
                  (.cmp (laneDirectionY ln2R) .eq (laneDirectionY lnR)))))))

/-- s7: the subject, a vehicle or a combination and a member of traffic, is moving on a highway on
    which two or more lanes are available for traffic moving in its direction. -/
def movingOnMultiLaneHighway : Formula :=
  .and (.or (vehicleAggregate vV) (combinationAggregate vV))
    (.and (.not (standstill vV))
      (.and (trafficAggregate vV)
        (.existsRegion (.lit "highway") "hw"
          (.and (.atom "st_highway" [hwR] [])
            (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln"
              (.and (.atom "st_lane" [lnR] [])
                (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, lnR] [])
                  (.and (.atom "st_on_way" [lnR, hwR] [])
                        twoOrMoreLanesInDirection))))))))

/-- Applicability: s2 (trigger): which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,; s5 (condition): so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,; s6 (exception): but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.; s7 (exception): This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction. -/
def applicability : Formula :=
  .and followsWideTruck
    (.and (.not overtakingAnyVehicle) (.not movingOnMultiLaneHighway))

/-- s3: the road users that occupy a roadway of the subject's and lie in the space between the
    subject and the road user `u` it follows. `count` reads no value of its term, so the term is
    zero. -/
def interveningUsers (u : Arg) : Term :=
  .aggregate .count "w"
    (.and (.not (.same wW vV))
      (.and (.not (.same wW u))
        (.and (.existsRegion (.lit "roadway") "rd"
                (.and (.atom "st_roadway" [rdR] [])
                  (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, rdR] [])
                        (.atom "rel_occupies" [wW, rdR] []))))
          (.and (aheadInLane wW vV)
                (.cmp (gapAhead vV wW) .lt (gapAhead vV u))))))
    zeroMetres

/-- s3: no obstruction lies on the highway the subject's lane lies on (the narrowing declared
    below: the claimed atoms place no region within the space itself). -/
def noObstructionOnTheWay : Formula :=
  .not (.existsRegion (.lit "highway") "hw2"
    (.and (.atom "st_highway" [hw2R] [])
      (.and (.existsRegion (.lit "lane") "ln3"
              (.and (.atom "st_lane" [ln3R] [])
                (.and (.atom "rel_occupies" [vV, ln3R] [])
                      (.atom "st_on_way" [ln3R, hw2R] []))))
            (.existsRegion (.lit "obstruction") "ob"
              (.and (.atom "st_obstruction" [obR] [])
                    (.atom "st_on_way" [obR, hw2R] []))))))

/-- s3 (the operationalization "whenever conditions permit"). The convention's third leaf, that no
    `dev.temporary_traffic_control` lies in the space, is not written: see the header and
    `task_result.md` — the node claims no atom that ties a device to the subject or to a region, so
    a device quantifier would range over every device of the scene. -/
def conditionsPermit (u : Arg) : Formula :=
  .and (.cmp (speedOf vV) .ge pConditionsPermitMinSpeed)
    (.and (.cmp (interveningUsers u) .le pConditionsPermitMaxInterveningUsers)
          noObstructionOnTheWay)

/-- Obligation: s3 (standard): shall, whenever conditions permit,; s4 (obligation): leave a space of 500 feet -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallUser "u"
    (.implies
      (.and (.not (.same vV uU))
        (.and (truckOrWideCombination uU)
          (.and (following vV uU) (aheadInLane uU vV))))
      (.implies (conditionsPermit uU) (.cmp (gapAhead vV uU) .ge fiveHundredFeet)))

def rule : Rule :=
  { id := "NRS_484B_127_2"
    laws := ["NRS-484B-127-2"]
    binders :=
      [ { name := "v", cls := clsV } ]
    applicability := applicability
    obligation := obligation
    assumptions := []
    intentions := []
    operationalizations :=
      [ { standard := "whenever conditions permit"
          concepts := ["dev.temporary_traffic_control", "kin.speed", "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane", "rel.occupies", "rel.surface_gap", "st.obstruction", "st.roadway"]
          params := ["p.conditions_permit_min_speed", "p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users"]
          convention := "Traffic-flow feasibility convention (free-flow versus congested operation in highway capacity practice): leaving and holding a long space ahead is possible only where the stream runs freely and nothing occupies the space. The conditions permit at an observation where the subject's kin.speed, “magnitude of velocity”, is at least p.conditions_permit_min_speed, so that a queue or stop-and-go running is not read as a failure to leave the space; and where the number of road users that occupy the subject's roadway (rel.occupies with st.roadway) between the subject and the vehicle it follows, read through the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap and rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, is at most p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users, so that a vehicle that has moved into the space is not read as the subject's closing of it; and where no st.obstruction, “a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user”, and no dev.temporary_traffic_control, “cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction”, lies in that space, since a works zone or a blocked lane makes the space impossible to hold. Both magnitudes are parameters of the reading; the words state none."
          surrogate := false } ]

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_127_2.

  The world. One straight east–west highway (region 10, the whole way between its boundary lines,
  y from −12 m to +12 m), an improved roadway on it (region 13) and lanes on it: region 11, the
  eastbound lane (y from −4 m to 0, direction east), region 12, the westbound lane (y from 0 to
  +4 m, direction west), and, where a scene needs a second lane of the subject's direction, region
  14 (y from −8 m to −4 m, direction east). Every lane and the roadway record the highway as their
  way. On the two-lane highway each lane records ordinal 1 of a count of 1 lane in its direction,
  so the count of s7 is decided, not merely unobserved.

  The bodies. An articulated lorry is 18 m long and 2.5 m wide (half-extents 9 m, 1.25 m, 2 m) and
  carries the truck and trailer-or-combination classes, so the truck aggregate holds of it; a
  passenger car is 4.8 m long and 1.78 m (70 inches) wide; a van is 5 m long and 1.8 m wide. All
  run in the eastbound lane on its centre line (y = −2 m), headings east.

  The instants. Each trace is three observations one second apart, the scene unchanged: the rule
  looks back nowhere, so no window needs padding and no witness names one.

  The figures that matter against the reading: a centre spacing of 60 m between two lorries is a
  longitudinal clearance of 42 m, far below the 500 feet (152.4 m) of s4; a centre spacing of
  260 m is a clearance of 242 m, far above it. 22 m/s is far above the free-flow bound of the
  conditions, 2 m/s and 0 m/s far below it. Every figure here is the witness's own and appears
  nowhere in the rule.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_127_2
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_127_2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n
def mps (n : Int) : Q := Units.metresPerSecond n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: v ↦ 1

/-- A lateral strip of the way, from `y0` to `y1`, running 2 km either side of the origin. -/
def strip (y0 y1 : Q) : List Vec :=
  [(m (-2000), y0), (m 2000, y0), (m 2000, y1), (m (-2000), y1)]

/-- Region 10: the whole highway between its boundary lines. -/
def highwayWay : Structure := Build.region 10 .highway (strip (m (-12)) (m 12))

/-- Region 11: the eastbound lane, with the lane ordinal and the count of lanes in its direction
    as the source records them. -/
def eastLane (ordinal count : Option Nat) : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 11 (strip (m (-4)) Q.zero) Build.east (ordinal := ordinal) (count := count) with
      ways := some [10] }

/-- Region 12: the westbound lane of a two-lane, two-way highway. -/
def westLane : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 12 (strip Q.zero (m 4)) Build.west (ordinal := some 1) (count := some 1) with
      ways := some [10] }

/-- Region 14: a second eastbound lane, of the same direction of travel as region 11. -/
def secondEastLane : Structure :=
  { Build.lane 14 (strip (m (-8)) (m (-4))) Build.east with ways := some [10] }

/-- Region 13: the improved roadway. -/
def roadwayOf (y0 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
  { Build.region 13 .roadway (strip y0 y1) with ways := some [10] }

/-- Region 15: a barrier standing in the eastbound lane, on the way. -/
def barrier : Structure :=
  { Build.rect 15 .obstruction (m 30) (m (-3)) (m 33) (m (-1)) with
      ways := some [10], obstructionKind := some .barrier }

/-- The two-lane, two-way highway: one lane in each direction. -/
def twoWayWorld : List Structure :=
  [highwayWay, eastLane (some 1) (some 1), westLane, roadwayOf (m (-4)) (m 4)]

/-- A carriageway whose lane adjacency records three lanes in the subject's direction. -/
def threeLaneWorld : List Structure :=
  [highwayWay, eastLane (some 2) (some 3), roadwayOf (m (-4)) (m 4)]

/-- Two lanes of the subject's direction on the way, neither recording a lane count. -/
def twoSameDirectionLanesWorld : List Structure :=
  [highwayWay, eastLane none none, secondEastLane, roadwayOf (m (-8)) Q.zero]

def lorry (track : TrackId) (x speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track [.truck, .trailerOrCombination] (x, m (-2)) Build.east speed (m 9, cm 125, m 2)

/-- The same lorry, of which the source records no body extent, so the space between the bodies
    cannot be read. -/
def bodylessLorry (track : TrackId) (x speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.withKin (lorry track x speed) fun k => { k with extent := none }

def car (track : TrackId) (x speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track [.motorVehicle] (x, m (-2)) Build.east speed (cm 240, cm 89, cm 75)

def vanUser (track : TrackId) (x speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track [.motorVehicle] (x, m (-2)) Build.east speed (cm 250, cm 90, m 1)

/-- Three observations a second apart of one unchanging scene. -/
def still (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) (devices : List Device) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun _k t => Build.scene t (some 1) users structures devices

/-- `forbid` (violated): On a two-lane rural highway with one lane in each direction, an articulated lorry runs at 22 m/s about 60 m behind another articulated lorry in the same lane, headings aligned. No road user is between them, no works or obstruction lies in the space, and the subject is well above the free-flow speed, so the conditions permit; the longitudinal gap is far below 500 feet. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `permit` (compliant): The same two lorries on the same highway at the same speed, but the follower holds a longitudinal gap of about 260 m, which exceeds 500 feet. -/
def permitTrace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 260) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): A passenger car — neither a truck of the truck aggregate nor a coupled combination, and 70 inches wide — follows an articulated lorry at 60 m on the same two-lane highway. The subject is outside the classes the subsection binds and the rule does not engage. -/
def idleTrace : Trace :=
  still [car 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `blind` (unknown): The forbid scene with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: both road users' classes, the following relation and the single-lane carriageway are recorded, but the space cannot be read, so the duty is unknown. -/
def blindTrace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), bodylessLorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_1` (not_applicable): The same two lorries at 60 m, moving on a dual carriageway whose lane adjacency records three lanes in their direction of travel. The second exception applies by its own words and the subsection does not apply. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] threeLaneWorld []

/-- `branch_2` (not_applicable): On the two-lane highway the following lorry is overtaking and passing the lorry ahead: the two travel in the same direction, the follower's speed exceeds the leader's by 4 m/s and the lorry ahead is still ahead of it in the lane as it passes. The first exception applies and the duty does not bite on the closed space. -/
def branch_2Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 26), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_3` (compliant): The follower lorry is held at 2 m/s in a slow-moving queue on the two-lane highway, 10 m behind the lorry ahead, with a van that has moved into the space between them. Its speed is below the free-flow bound and a road user occupies the space, so the conditions do not permit and no space of 500 feet is owed at that observation. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 2), vanUser 3 (m 14) (mps 2), lorry 2 (m 28) (mps 2)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_4` (not_applicable): The two lorries on a way that records no lane count, but on which
    a second lane of their direction of travel lies beside theirs: two lanes are available for
    traffic moving in the same direction, so the second exception applies. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoSameDirectionLanesWorld []

/-- `branch_5` (compliant): The forbid scene at free-flow speed with a van that has moved into the
    space 20 m ahead of the subject: a road user occupies the space, so the conditions do not
    permit although the stream runs freely. -/
def branch_5Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), vanUser 3 (m 20) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_6` (compliant): The forbid geometry with both lorries creeping at 2 m/s and nothing in
    the space: the subject's speed alone is below the free-flow bound, so the conditions do not
    permit. -/
def branch_6Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 2), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 2)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_7` (compliant): The forbid scene with a barrier standing on the way ahead: an
    obstruction makes the space impossible to hold, so the conditions do not permit. -/
def branch_7Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] (twoWayWorld ++ [barrier]) []

/-- `branch_8` (not_applicable): The subject lorry leads and the other lorry runs 60 m behind it:
    the subject follows nothing, so the subsection never engages. -/
def branch_8Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), lorry 2 (m (-60)) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_9` (not_applicable): The subject lorry follows a passenger car 70 inches wide at 60 m:
    the road user followed is neither a truck of the aggregate nor a wide combination, so the
    subsection does not engage. -/
def branch_9Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 22), car 2 (m 60) (mps 22)] twoWayWorld []

/-- `branch_10` (compliant): Both lorries stand still on the three-lane carriageway, 60 m apart:
    the subject is not moving, so the second exception does not apply by its own words, and the
    duty engages — but a standing subject is below the free-flow bound, so the conditions do not
    permit. -/
def branch_10Trace : Trace :=
  still [lorry 1 (m 0) (mps 0), lorry 2 (m 60) (mps 0)] threeLaneWorld []

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_127_2"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("v", 1)]
    expected := expected
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["rel.surface_gap"]
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_5" branch_5Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_6" branch_6Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_7" branch_7Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_8" branch_8Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_9" branch_9Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_10" branch_10Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_11" branch_11Trace .compliant ]

end TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_127_2

/-
  NRS_484B_127_2 — NRS-484B-127-2

  THE READING (the blueprint's; the coding session records here, per span, how each element,
  operationalization and composition below is written, and every choice the text did not dictate).

  Spans:
    s1 (subject): The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
    s2 (trigger): which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
    s3 (standard): shall, whenever conditions permit,
    s4 (obligation): leave a space of 500 feet
    s5 (condition): so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,
    s6 (exception): but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.
    s7 (exception): This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.

  Elements (span → atoms, derived):
    s1: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'kin.extent'], derived []
    s2: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'kin.extent'], derived ['drv.interaction.following']
    s4: atoms ['rel.surface_gap', 'rel.ahead_behind_in_lane'], derived []
    s6: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle'], derived ['drv.interaction.overtaking']
    s7: atoms ['ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles', 'ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic', 'st.highway', 'st.lane', 'st.lane_adjacency', 'st.lane_direction', 'st.on_way', 'rel.occupies'], derived ['drv.motion.standstill']

  Literals the text states (each written through its Units constructor):
    s1: 80 in — 80 inches
    s2: 80 in — 80 inches
    s4: 500 ft — 500 feet
    s7: 2 count — two

  No magnitude below is this file's own: parameters name the reading, literals are the text's.

  HOW EACH SPAN IS WRITTEN

  s1 (the binder's class, `clsV`). `truckOrWideCombination v`: the admitted aggregate
  DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, or the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles
  with the read width (`kin_extent`, component `width`, which the vocabulary reads as the full
  width) at least the text's 80 inches. The qualifier "80 inches or more in overall width" is
  attached to the combination limb, as the record's `applicability` states it. "The driver of" is
  the record's own observable reading (agency) and is not restated in `narrowings`.

  s2 (`followsWideTruck`, in the applicability). Some road user other than the subject
  (`.not (.same v u)`) is itself a truck of that aggregate or a combination of that width, and the
  subject is following it (`drv.interaction.following`, the same-direction tolerance of the
  reading). The followed road user is quantified, not bound: the duty exists for the subject
  whether or not a scene supplies one.

  s3 (`conditionsPermit`, the operationalization, in the obligation). The subject's `kin_speed`
  at least `p.conditions_permit_min_speed`; the count of other road users that occupy a roadway
  the subject occupies (`st.roadway` with `rel.occupies`), lie ahead of the subject in its lane
  (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`) and lie nearer than the followed road user (the longitudinal
  component of `rel.surface_gap`), at most `p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users`; and no
  `st.obstruction` on the way (see the narrowing below). The convention's fourth leaf, that no
  `dev.temporary_traffic_control` lies in the space, is not written at all: the node claims no atom
  that relates a device to the subject or to a region (`dev.governs` and `dev.position` are atoms
  of the surface, and this node claims neither), so a device quantifier would range over every
  device of the scene, the subject's or not. That is a defect of the node's mapping, not a reading
  open to me, and it is reported rather than declared here.

  s4 (the obligation). For every road user the subject is following in the sense of s2 and that is
  ahead of it in its lane (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`, the s4 claim that fixes which space is
  meant), where the conditions of s3 permit, the longitudinal component of `rel.surface_gap`
  between the two bodies is at least the text's 500 feet. The obligation re-selects the followed
  road user with the whole of s2's selection, since the applicability's binding does not reach it.
  The record's reading of "a space of 500 feet" as that longitudinal clearance is the plan's
  narrowing on s4 and is not restated here.

  s5 is the record's residue: no verdict turns on it.

  s6 (`overtakingAnyVehicle`, negated in the applicability). Some road user other than the subject
  is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or a combination of DEF-NRS-484A-050, and the subject
  is passing it (`drv.interaction.overtaking`, with the reading's same-direction tolerance and
  minimum speed excess). The overtaking road user is the subject, whose class s1 already fixes.

  s7 (`movingOnMultiLaneHighway`, negated in the applicability). The subject is a vehicle or a
  combination; it is not at a standstill (`drv.motion.standstill`, the posted definition of a
  complete cessation from movement, negated for "while moving"); it is traffic
  (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), which fixes whose movement the lanes are available for; and it
  occupies (`rel.occupies`) a lane (`st.lane`) that lies on a highway (`st.on_way`, `st.highway`)
  on which two or more lanes run in that lane's direction of travel. The last is read from the two
  observations the claimed atoms carry of that one fact: the lane's recorded count of lanes in its
  direction (`st.lane_adjacency`, field `count`) is at least the text's two, or another lane on the
  same highway carries the same direction of travel (`st.lane_direction`, both components). Either
  observation establishes the fact the words state; neither adds a requirement to it, and the
  direction read is the one the subject travels in because it is the direction of the lane the
  subject occupies.

  THE READING I CHOSE (declared in `narrowings`)

  s3: "no obstruction lies in that space". The atoms the node claims for this standard carry no
  relation that places a structure region within the space between two bodies: `rel.occupies`
  relates a road user to a region, `rel.surface_gap` two road users, and the node claims no
  `st.region_geometry`. The leaf is therefore read at the coarsest place those atoms reach: an
  `st.obstruction` region that lies on the highway the subject's lane lies on makes the conditions
  not permit, so the reading relieves the duty in some scenes where the words would relieve it only
  for an obstruction in the space itself.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_127_2

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vV : Arg := .var "v"

/-- The quantified variables: the followed road user, an overtaken road user, a road user in the
    space, the highway and lanes of s7, the roadway and the obstruction of s3. -/
def uU : Arg := .var "u"
def wW : Arg := .var "w"
def hwR : Arg := .var "hw"
def lnR : Arg := .var "ln"
def ln2R : Arg := .var "ln2"
def hw2R : Arg := .var "hw2"
def ln3R : Arg := .var "ln3"
def rdR : Arg := .var "rd"
def obR : Arg := .var "ob"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/

# NRS_484B_127_2 — coding session result

## Final verdict

`UNUSED_CLAIM — dev_temporary_traffic_control`

The node is wrong on one point, and that point alone blocks the gate: the s3 operationalization
claims `dev.temporary_traffic_control` but claims no atom that ties a device to the subject or to a
region, so the claim cannot be written in a formula at all. Everything the gate checks before the
claim audit passes on the delivered files — the two files build, `Rule.check` is empty, the
soundness and scope checks pass, every quantified variable is anchored, the declarations match the
node, no span is unexpressed, and no unclaimed atom is read. The rule and the fifteen witnesses are
complete and delivered; the one leaf the node makes unwritable is the only thing missing.

## Gate runs (4 of 6 used)

| # | verdict | what I changed after it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `UNANCHORED_VARIABLE` — `ttc` | The s3 standard's "no works zone lies in that space" was written as `.existsDevice "temporary_traffic_control" "ttc" (dev_temporary_traffic_control ttc)`. The node claims no atom relating a device to the subject or a region, so the quantifier ranges over every device of the scene. I removed that leaf (keeping the obstruction leaf, which `rel.occupies` + `st.on_way` do anchor) so the gate could check the rest of the rule and the witnesses, and dropped the one witness (cones) that only that leaf moved. |
| 2 | `UNUSED_CLAIM` — `dev_temporary_traffic_control` | The gate's own message names `dev_governs` as the device anchor, and its parenthetical ("the record's claims are already checked") left open whether the claim audit reads atom families. One run to find out: I wrote the leaf as "no temporary traffic control governs a lane the subject occupies" (`dev_governs ttc ln4`, `ln4` anchored by `rel_occupies v ln4`) and re-added the cones witness. |
| 3 | `UNCLAIMED_ATOM` — `dev_governs` | Settled it: the claim audit is per atom id, so the leaf is unwritable either way (unanchored with the claimed atom, unclaimed with the anchoring atom). Reverted to the run-2 state, which is the correct deliverable: every name in the formulas is claimed (hard rule 3), and the node's defect is reported rather than worked around. |
| 4 | `UNUSED_CLAIM` — `dev_temporary_traffic_control` | Nothing; this is the delivered state and the verdict the harness will reproduce. |

The gate's verdicts are ordered, so runs 1–3 never reached the witness, adequacy or vacuity
stages, and no run of a satisfiable claim set exists to reach them: the witnesses below are
reasoned against Core's semantics (which I read: `Semantics.lean`, `Atoms.lean`, `RuleEval.lean`,
`Rule.lean`, `Manifest.lean`, `Builders.lean`, `Units.lean`), not confirmed by the gate.

## What the plan agent must change

**Span s3 (the operationalization "whenever conditions permit").** Its convention requires that
"no `dev.temporary_traffic_control` … lies in that space". `dev.temporary_traffic_control` is a
device-kind atom: the only way a formula reads a device is a device quantifier, and a device
quantifier is anchored to the subject only through `dev.governs` (device ↦ region) or `dev.position`
(device ↦ a comparison with a place). The node claims neither, and no other claimed atom takes a
device argument. One of two repairs:

- add `dev.governs` (and, for the obstruction, `st.region_geometry`) to the s3 operationalization's
  `concepts`, so the works-zone leaf can be placed — with `dev.governs` the leaf reads "no
  temporary traffic control governs a lane the subject occupies", which the gate accepted as
  anchored in run 3; or
- drop `dev.temporary_traffic_control` from s3 and leave the standard to speed and the intervening
  users, with the obstruction leaf as written here.

This is a defect of the node's mapping and not a `no_atom` gap: the surface does carry atoms for
the words (`dev.governs`, `dev.position`), the node simply does not claim them, so by hard rule 2 I
neither declared `no_atom` on s3 nor wrote the words with an unclaimed atom.

**Two further defects of the node that do not block the gate but make leaves that no witness can
move** (reported, not worked around; I did not delete either atom):

1. `ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles` **can never be true.** The run's reading
   admits that aggregate with *no* included class and sixteen unresolved ones, so
   `aggregateMembership` returns `unknown` for any road user carrying one of those sixteen classes

further run of mine could reach the witness or vacuity stages, so two runs of the budget are left
unspent. The files are delivered complete apart from that leaf, with the defect, the two reading
defects and every choice I made recorded here and in the rule's header and `narrowings`.
